questions.q: Why was Trevor Noah's existence a crime under apartheid?
a: His father was white and his mother was black
His family had entered the country illegally
His parents were not legally married
He was born outside a designated township
questions.why: Apartheid law banned interracial relationships, so his birth was evidence of one.

questions.q: What did Trevor's mother do when authorities came near?
a: She put him down and pretended he was not her child
She hid him in a neighbor's house
She told them he was adopted
She sent him to live with his father
questions.why: She had to be careful because his father could not be seen with him.

questions.q: What was the black tax Trevor's mother wanted him to avoid?
a: Money black children spend to make up for their parents' poverty
A fee charged by the government for black schools
The share of wages taken by tribal leaders
A payment required to register a black-owned business
questions.why: She spent her limited money on books and teaching him to escape that cycle.

questions.q: What happened when the Zulu bus driver argued with Trevor's mother?
a: She forced the door open and they jumped out
She convinced the driver to let them stay on
She paid him extra to finish the route
She called the police from the bus
questions.why: The driver sped up to trap them, so she grabbed her sons and ran home.

questions.q: How did Trevor's ability to blend in help his tuckshop business?
a: He could sell to students from every group and navigate between them
He could buy stock at a lower price from wholesalers
He could avoid paying the school for his stall
He could hire other students to sell for him
questions.why: His wit let him move among nerds, jocks and rich kids without trouble.
